 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Luca Williams-Barnett celebrates his first goal for Tottenham
 By Chris McKenna BBC Sport journalist Tottenham Hotspur teenager Luca Williams-Barnett starred for Roberto de Zerbi's side as they comfortably beat Ipswich Town. 
 On his first Premier League start, Williams-Barnett scored one and helped create the other for Dominic Solanke to give Spurs their fourth win of the season.
 Tottenham were on the front foot early on and Solanke went close with a couple of headers.
 But it took 18-year-old Williams-Barnett to break the deadlock in the 15th minute with his first senior goal. 
 It was sheer determination from the club's academy graduate as he got ahead of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and turn home to become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.
 Mohammed Kudus then struck the post with a free-kick while Williams-Barnett and James Maddison - back in the team for the first time since 24 October - forced saves from Christian Walton in the Ipswich goal before the break.
 Julio Enciso was one of the Tractor Boys' bright sparks but, despite some tidy trickery on the ball, he couldn't create many openings as Antonin Kinsky remained largely untroubled in the Spurs goal.
 Tottenham got their second six minutes into the second half thanks to some great wing play down the left from Williams-Barnett.
 The teenager crossed for Solanke to turn home just his second leg goal of the season, with manager De Zerbi watching on from the stands as he served a touchline ban. 
 Williams-Barnett was given a standing ovation when substituted in the 64th minute.
 Tottenham cruised to the win as Gary O'Neil's Ipswich suffered their sixth defeat of the season.
 Tottenham analysis: De Zerbi rewarded for faith in youth 
 Figure caption, Roberto de Zerbi post-match interview - Tottenham Hotspur 2-0 Ipswich Town
 Williams-Barnett had played just nine Premier League minutes before De Zerbi boldly put him in for his first start here.
 The Luton-born winger, who look assured from the first moments, showed energy and eagerness to get on the ball, and became the sixth youngest Tottenham player to start a Premier League match.
 Williams-Barnett, who joined Spurs aged 10, also featured in the EFL Cup this season as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.
 While his goal didn't have the best-looking finish and was more about just putting his body ahead of Ouattara, it showed his determination.
 The cross for Solanke's goal was a display of creativeness and his performance had the home fans singing about him being "one of our own". 
 He's the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale did so at the age of 18 in 2007.
 De Zerbi's decision to bring him in was rewarded and it was a real show of faith in the club's youth as they claimed their fourth win in their last five outings.
 What did you make of Tottenham’s display? 
 Ipswich analysis: Leaky defence has Tractor Boys sinking 
 Figure caption, Gary O'Neil post-match interview - Tottenham Hotspur 2-0 Ipswich Town
 Ipswich have now conceded in 30 straight Premier League games stretching back to their previous time in the division - a record only West Brom, Blackburn, Wolves and Watford have matched in the past.
 The fact they've not kept a single clean sheet this term and only Crystal Palace have conceded more than their 22 goals suggests one reason for their struggles.
 They are now without a win since their 2-1 victory over Fulham on 10 October – a five-game run - and they are just two points above the relegation zone.
 Another worry for O'Neil is that they have conceded five goals in the first 15 minutes of the second half with only Palace and Sunderland doing worse in those moments. 
 O'Neil must find a way to sort out their leaky defence if they want to avoid returning to the Championship.
